newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Network Entertainment out of administration.
newsitem.headline: Network Entertainment out of administration.

text.p: Video publisher and distributor Network Entertainment Group Ltd said on Wednesday it has been released from administration after a capital injection from a company associated with the Waterhouse racing family.
William Waterhouse, his son Robert Waterhouse and Gaye Karele would become directors of Network Entertainment, the company said in a statement.

"The company's obligations to its bank have been released and new funding, adequate for the company's purposes, has been arranged by certain of the new directors who join the board today," it said in a statement.
Subject to shareholder approval, a company associated with those directors would be issued 70 million new shares in Network Entertainment at one cent par value each, it said.
Network currently has 20.2 million shares on issue.
The company's creditors last week gave it a reprieve from full liquidation when they voted to allow the administrator to sell its business under a deed of company arrangement.
However creditors were reported in local media to face a maximum payout of 10 cents in the dollar.
Network last traded on July 15 at 11 cents, giving it a market capitalisation of A$2.2 million.
The company listed just eight and a half months ago, but by February it was warning that it would not meet profit forecasts contained in its prospectus due to weaker than expected sales.
It halved its earnings forecast and then announced in May it would be unlikely to meet the revised target.
Network said on July 1 it expected to report a net loss for the year to June 30, citing continuing weak trading conditions and abnormally high product returns by retailers.
The shares were suspended on July 16.
